A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoCoDL research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across the changed pagination.

before.justification: Section 4 and Figures 1–4 report original logistic-regression convergence experiments on diabetes, a5a, australian and w1a.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, and Appendix B adds original results on covtype.binary, MNIST and synthetic Dirichlet data.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same primal-dual updates, control variates, probabilistic communication and unbiased compression. The adaptation for g = 0 in Section 3.1 is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix B adds covtype.binary, MNIST classification of 7s versus 8s, and synthetic Dirichlet data with varying heterogeneity. All four original datasets remain. This substantially broadens data and scenario coverage while retaining regularized logistic regression.

E2.justification: Corresponding original experiments retain ADIANA, DIANA, 5GCS-CC, CompressedScaffnew, GradSkip and Scaffold. The added experiments compare against the already evaluated ADIANA; no new comparator is introduced.

E3.justification: Existing experimental settings remain unchanged. Added configurations include covtype.binary with 6, 100 and 6,000 clients, MNIST with 6 clients, and a controlled Dirichlet comparison using alpha = 1 and 10, n = 100, d = 10 and one sample per client.

E4.justification: Appendix B and Figure 7 add a focused sensitivity study asking how heterogeneity affects LoCoDL and ADIANA convergence. It compares two Dirichlet concentration settings and reports little difference. The earlier compressor and client-count comparisons remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical tests. The new statement of 'no significant difference' across alpha values is not accompanied by a statistical procedure.

E6.justification: The original plot panels are unchanged: v1 Figures 1–4 correspond to v2 Figures 2, 1, 4 and 3. New Figures 5–7 substantially extend the results, showing LoCoDL's communication advantage over ADIANA on covtype.binary and MNIST and reporting little sensitivity to alpha in the synthetic experiment.

T1.justification: Assumptions 1.1 and 2.1, Theorem 3.1, Corollary 3.2, the complexity tables and the complete Appendix A proof retain the same mathematics. Changes to equation numbering and display arrangement are presentational.

C1.justification: The abstract and main contributions retain the same scope: combining local training with generic unbiased compression, proving doubly accelerated communication complexity under strong convexity, and demonstrating empirical advantages. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: The conclusion adds a possible general-convex analysis using objective gaps and explains uncertainty about variance-reduced local training in nonconvex settings. This expands the existing nonconvex caveat. Appendix B also introduces an interpretation of Dirichlet concentration as controlling heterogeneity.

D1.justification: v2 adds a LibSVM license statement and documents synthetic-data generation and the MNIST class selection. A new reproducibility ambiguity remains: Appendix B says both methods use rand-1 in the best combination, whereas Figure 7 labels ADIANA as rand-2.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on downlink compression and nonconvex compression/local training, including Dorfman, Huang, Chen, Yi and Meinhardt, plus LeCun for MNIST. These extend the discussion locally; the central positioning against existing communication-efficient methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. Limited editing updates publication and author information, moves the contents list to the appendix, expands the concluding discussion and introduces Appendix B for additional experiments.

P2.justification: The conference format substantially changes typography, spacing, equation and algorithm displays, and figure sizing and placement. Tables 1–2 are grouped together, existing figures are reordered, australian moves to the appendix, and Figures 5–7 add six plot panels.

improvement.justification: Appendix B broadens empirical validation beyond v1's four tabular datasets, particularly through covtype.binary and MNIST, while preserving the original results and proof. The expanded applicability discussion also helps. These gains are limited by the narrow heterogeneity study, absent uncertainty reporting and its inconsistent ADIANA compressor description.
